I've been farming these 22 mu in Quzhou since I was 17 years old. I'm 52 now. My husband works construction over in Handan, and my son and daughter-in-law both have jobs at a factory, so most days it's just me and my younger daughter handling the fields. My husband comes back when it's really busy — harvest, planting — but I make the day-to-day decisions.

We grow cotton on 12 mu. That's always been our main money crop. Another 7 mu has winter wheat in it right now — I planted it last October — and the minute that wheat comes off in June, maize goes into the same ground. You can't waste even three days in that window. The last 3 mu or so I started growing stevia on, because my sister-in-law's family has been doing it for two years and the buyer comes right to the village with cash. I'm still learning that crop, though.

**Cotton:** I buy hybrid seed from the seed station, about 60 yuan per mu. I hire Old Wang's tractor to plow the ground first — same as every year. At planting in mid-April, I put down half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, about 25 kg, and when the cotton starts flowering in July I topdress with another 10–12 kg of urea per mu. Li Sao down the road tried cutting back on fertilizer last year and her cotton was short and stubby, so I'm not making that mistake. The pump electricity keeps going up, so I only irrigate twice — once right after planting to settle the seedlings, and again when the bolls are forming. Cotton always needs spray. Bollworm will ruin you if you're lazy. I put herbicide down before the weeds get bad, and I watch for insects all summer. Picking is the hard part. My family helps, but for 12 mu I have to hire women from the village to pick. I expect about 280 kg per mu if the weather holds.

**Wheat:** The 7 mu is greening up now. I gave it base fertilizer last October when I sowed it — compound fertilizer, about 25 kg per mu. In March I already topdressed with urea when it was jointing. I'll irrigate it one more time before harvest in early June if the rain doesn't come. Maybe spray a little fungicide if I see rust on the leaves. Should get about 420 kg per mu, about the same as last year.

**Maize:** Right after the wheat comes off in mid-June, Old Wang plants the maize with his tractor. I buy new hybrid seed every year — saved seed doesn't work for maize — about 50 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, and when the maize is knee-high I side-dress urea. I irrigate twice if the summer is dry — once at planting to get it up, and once at tasseling. Herbicide for the weeds, and I watch for armyworm. Yield should be around 480 kg per mu.

**Stevia:** The 3 mu I plant with seedlings in late April. I don't know stevia as well as the others. I put some chicken manure and a little compound fertilizer — maybe 15 kg per mu — and side-dress once more after the first cut. It needs water but not as much as cotton. Two irrigations. Picking and drying is all hand work, so it's just family labor. I hope to get about 200 kg of dried leaves per mu.

The hardest part is the money. Fertilizer prices went up again, and diesel for the pump isn't cheap either. I'm spending about 12,500 yuan on all the inputs this year. If cotton prices stay at 7–8 yuan per jin, we'll be alright, but there's never much cushion. I'd rather put a bit too much fertilizer than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and I've seen too many bad years.
